parts.label: (b)
parts.note: Both explanations make the same point: $1120 = 8 × $140 is simple interest on the original $5600, whereas compound interest is calculated on a growing amount so every year after the first earns more than $140 (year 2 earns $143.50). Actual total 5600(1.025^8 − 1) ≈ $1223.06, confirming the claim.

key_verdict: No disagreement; the setter's key is correct in both parts and the explanation in (b) is the one a marker would credit.
why: A 3-mark compound-interest question with a two-step calculation and a one-mark explain-why on a common misconception is exactly the weight and shape SEAB used at Q5 in 2023, but the skills are different: the interest of ONE later year is not asked in any exemplar, the misconception targeted is simple-versus-compound over 8 years rather than monthly-versus-yearly, and the parts run calculate-then-explain; every money value lands on exact cents and the register (Calculate ..., Explain why ...) is the paper's own.
